s: 当ホテルのプールをご利用の（　　）は、必ず水泳帽を着用してください。
en: When using the hotel pool, please be sure to wear a swimming cap.
why: 〜の際は is the formal 'when' that notices use for an official action like ご利用. It takes a noun with の.
〜最中 is the middle of a short activity that gets interrupted. A pool rule is not about an interruption.
〜次第 'as soon as' takes a verb stem (利用し次第). It cannot follow a noun with の.
名の限り means 'to the very limit' (力の限り). It makes no sense with ご利用.
tell: Notice + ご〜の + は + a rule: the formal 'when' is 〜の際は.

s: お車で（　　）、近くの有料駐車場をご利用ください。
en: If you are coming by car, please use one of the paid car parks nearby.
c: ご来場になったとたん
ご来場になったかと思うと
why: ご〜の際は is the set notice phrase for 'when you do X'. A polite request (ご利用ください) follows it naturally.
〜たとたん reports a surprise that has already happened. It cannot be followed by a request like ご利用ください.
〜たかと思うと describes something you watched happen. It cannot be followed by a request like ご利用ください.
〜最中 needs an activity with some length (会議の最中). Arriving happens in a moment, so it has no middle.
tell: Notice + a request to guests: ご〜の際は. とたん and かと思うと report past events and cannot take a request.

s: このたびの事故（　　）、多くの皆様にご迷惑をおかけしたことを深くお詫び申し上げます。
en: We deeply apologise to everyone for the trouble caused by this accident.
why: 〜に際して is a neutral 'on the occasion of'. It also works for an unplanned, unwelcome event like an accident.
〜にあたって is for a milestone you plan and take on (開店・就任・出発). Nobody plans an accident, so it cannot take にあたって.
〜に限り is the 'only' of notices and shop offers (本日に限り). 'Only for this accident' makes no sense in an apology.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place (三か月にわたって). An accident is an event, not a span.
tell: An unplanned, unwelcome event (事故・災害): に際して. にあたって needs a milestone you take on.

s: 新しい支店を開設する（　　）、地元の方々を招いて記念式典を行った。
en: On opening the new branch, we invited local people and held a ceremony to mark it.
why: 〜にあたって marks a one-off, deliberate milestone like opening a branch. It takes a noun or a dictionary-form verb.
〜とたんに needs the た形 (開設したとたん), and it brings an unexpected result, not a planned ceremony.
〜限り 'as long as' links two lasting states. Opening a branch is a one-off action, not a state.
〜だけ 'as much as' repeats the same verb (食べたいだけ食べる). It has no 'on the occasion of' meaning.
tell: A one-off milestone, then a planned action because of it: 〜にあたって.

s: 私は疲れてベッドに（　　）、すぐに深い眠りに落ちてしまった。
en: Exhausted, the instant I got into bed, I fell fast asleep.
why: 〜たとたん(に): the instant you did something, a surprise followed. It works for your own action.
〜かと思うと is only for watching someone or something else. Here the subject is 私.
〜にあたって marks a one-off milestone (starting a job, opening a shop). Going to bed is not one.
〜最中に means 'in the middle of' an activity, and needs ている形 or a noun: 入っている最中.
tell: Your own sudden action plus an unexpected result: たとたん, not かと思うと.

s: 私は冷房の効いた店から外に（　　）、眼鏡が真っ白にくもってしまった。
en: The instant I stepped out of the air-conditioned shop, my glasses fogged up completely.
why: 〜たとたん: the instant you did something, a surprise followed. It works for your own action, as here.
〜かと思うと describes someone or something else you are watching. It is never used for the speaker's own action (私は).
〜次第 'as soon as' must be followed by a plan or a request, never a past event. Foggy glasses were not planned.
〜最中 needs an activity with some length. Stepping outside takes a moment, so it has no middle.
tell: Your own instant action plus an unplanned result: 〜たとたん. かと思うと is only for others.

s: テレビをつけた（　　）、大きな地震のニュースが目に飛び込んできた。
en: The moment I turned on the TV, news of a big earthquake jumped out at me.
why: た形 + とたん: right after a quick action, something unexpected happened. Shocking news fits.
〜次第 takes the verb stem (つけ次第), not the た形. It also cannot describe a past surprise.
〜以来 takes the て形 (つけて以来) and needs a state that lasts until now. One moment of news is not that.
〜た上で is a careful first step that leads to a planned second step. News you did not expect is not planned.
tell: た形 plus a sudden, unplanned event right after: 〜たとたん.

s: うちの娘は、さっきまで大声で泣いていた（　　）、もうけろりとして笑っている。
en: My daughter was bawling a minute ago, and now she is laughing as if nothing happened.
why: 〜かと思うと: you watch someone else do X, then at once something quite different. It accepts 〜ていた before it.
〜とたん needs a one-moment verb in た形 (泣き出したとたん). 泣いていた is an ongoing state, so the connection fails.
〜最中に means an activity was interrupted while still going on. Here the crying is already over.
〜次第 takes a verb stem and must be followed by a plan or a request. It cannot follow 泣いていた.
tell: Someone else flips fast from X to Y (さっきまで〜ていた → もう〜): 〜かと思うと.

s: 隣の部屋の子どもたちは、やっと（　　）、また騒ぎ始めた。
en: The kids in the next room finally went quiet, and then straight away they started making noise again.
c: 静かになったかと思ったら
why: 〜たかと思ったら: you watch others do X, and the next moment Y. The kids are someone else, so it fits.
〜た上で is a careful first step before a planned second step. Nobody planned this noise.
〜うちに (change) describes a slow change while something goes on. 'While getting quiet, they got loud' contradicts itself, and the change here is sudden.
〜次第 must be followed by a plan or a request, never a past event like 騒ぎ始めた.
tell: Watching others: X, then at once back to Y. 〜たかと思ったら.

s: A「新しく入った佐藤さん、どう？」B「それが、やっと仕事に（　　）、来月辞めるって言うんですよ。」
en: A: How is Sato, the new hire? B: Well, just when he seemed to be getting used to the job, he says he is quitting next month.
c: 慣れてきたかと思ったら
why: 〜たかと思ったら: B watches someone else (佐藤さん) reach X, and then something unexpected comes at once.
〜次第 means 'as soon as X, I will do Y'. It cannot report a surprise that someone else sprang on you.
〜うちに (change) is followed by a slow change that crept in. Announcing he will quit is a sudden, deliberate statement.
〜て以来 must be followed by a state that has lasted until now. 来月辞める is about the future, which 以来 does not allow.
tell: Someone else reaches X, then a surprise at once: 〜たかと思ったら.

s: 終了のチャイムが（　　）、学生たちは一斉に教室を飛び出していった。
en: Almost before the end-of-class chime had rung, the students rushed out of the classroom all at once.
c: 鳴るか鳴らないかのうちに
why: 〜か〜ないかのうちに: the same verb, positive then negative. The next thing happens with almost no gap.
〜次第 must be followed by a plan or a request, never a past event like 飛び出していった.
〜つつ needs the same subject on both sides. The chime rings, but the students run.
〜た上で needs the same subject and a planned second step. A chime cannot prepare the students' exit.
tell: Y happens almost before X is over: same verb, then its ない形: 〜か〜ないかのうちに.

s: 息子は朝ごはんを食べ終わるか（　　）、かばんをつかんで玄関を飛び出していった。
en: My son had barely finished his breakfast before he grabbed his bag and dashed out the door.
c: 食べ終わらないかのうちに
食べ終わったかのうちに
食べ終わらなかったかのうちに
食べ終わるかのうちに
why: The shape is fixed: verb + か + the same verb in ない形 + かのうちに. 食べ終わるか食べ終わらないかのうちに.
The second verb must be negative. 食べ終わったか is positive and past, which breaks the fixed shape.
The negative half stays non-past: 食べ終わらない, not 食べ終わらなかった.
Repeating the positive verb (食べ終わるか食べ終わるか) is not the pattern. The second half must be negative.
tell: After 〜るか, the blank needs the same verb in ない形 + かのうちに.

s: 大事な商談を行っている（　　）、突然誰かの携帯電話が大きな音で鳴り出した。
en: Right in the middle of an important business meeting, someone's phone suddenly started ringing loudly.
why: ている + 最中に: right in the middle of a short activity, something unplanned broke in. 突然 is the signal.
〜限り 'as long as' links two lasting states, and no past tense may follow it. A phone that suddenly rang is neither.
〜つつ takes the ます stem (行いつつ), not ている, and needs the same subject. We hold the meeting, but the phone rings.
〜次第 takes the verb stem (行い次第), not ている, and must be followed by a plan or a request.
tell: ている + 最中に + something that suddenly breaks in (突然).

s: 社長がスピーチを（　　）、会場の照明が突然すべて消えてしまった。
en: Right in the middle of the president's speech, all the lights in the hall suddenly went out.
why: 〜ている最中に: right in the middle of an activity, something unplanned broke in. なさっている is the honorific of している.
〜つつ needs the same subject for both actions. The president speaks, but the lights go out.
〜次第 'as soon as' must be followed by a plan or a request, never a past event like 消えてしまった.
〜た上で is a careful first step and then a planned second step by the same person. A blackout is neither.
tell: Honorific ている形 + 最中に + a sudden interruption: なさっている最中に.

s: せっかく日本に留学しているのだから、日本に（　　）、できるだけ多くの観光地を訪れたい。
en: Since I have this chance to study in Japan, I want to visit as many sights as I can while I am still here.
why: 〜うちに (before it changes): act while the chance is still open. A wish like 訪れたい follows naturally.
〜たとたん bans a wish or intention after it, and いる is not a one-moment verb.
〜最中 is the middle of a short activity that gets interrupted. Being in Japan is a long state, not an activity.
〜て以来 is followed by a state that has lasted until now. A wish for the future (訪れたい) is not allowed after it.
tell: A window that will close (せっかく) + a wish or plan: 〜うちに.

s: 暗く（　　）、子どもたちを家に帰らせてください。
en: Please send the children home before it gets dark.
why: ない形 + うちに: do it before the change happens. A request like 帰らせてください is exactly what follows this うちに.
〜たとたん cannot be followed by a request like 〜てください.
Dictionary form + うちに here would mean 'while it was getting dark, a change crept in'. That うちに refuses a request after it.
〜最中 is the middle of an activity that gets interrupted. Getting dark is a natural change, not an activity.
tell: ない形 + うちに = before it changes, then a request: 暗くならないうちに.

s: このセールは明日までなので、在庫が（　　）早めに買っておいたほうがいいですよ。
en: This sale ends tomorrow, so you should buy early while there is still stock.
why: 〜うちに: do it while the chance is still there. Advice to act (買っておいたほうがいい) follows.
〜次第 means 'as soon as'. Buying 'as soon as the stock runs out' is impossible.
〜最中 needs an activity in progress (〜ている最中). ある is a plain state.
〜て以来 is followed by a state that lasts until now. Advice to act soon cannot follow it.
tell: A chance that will run out + advice to act now: 〜うちに.

s: 最初は苦手だった納豆も、毎朝（　　）、だんだんおいしく感じるようになってきた。
en: I used to dislike natto, but as I kept eating it every morning, I gradually came to find it tasty.
why: 〜ているうちに (change): while doing something for a while, a change crept in by itself. だんだん〜ようになってきた is that change.
〜最中に is followed by a sudden interruption. A slow change of taste over many mornings is not one.
〜たとたん marks one instant followed by a surprise. 毎朝 and だんだん describe a slow change over many mornings, so they clash.
〜次第 'as soon as' is followed by a plan or a request. だんだん shows a slow change, not a planned step.
tell: Doing X again and again, then だんだん a change crept in: 〜ているうちに.

s: ネットで調べものをしている（　　）、いつの間にか外が明るくなっていた。
en: While I was looking things up online, it got light outside before I knew it.
why: 〜ているうちに (change): while doing something, a change happened without your noticing. いつの間にか is the signal.
〜限り 'as long as' links a lasting condition to a lasting result. It cannot lead into a change that has already happened (明るくなっていた).
〜とたんに needs a one-moment verb in た形 (調べたとたん). It cannot follow ている.
〜次第 takes a verb stem and is followed by a plan or a request, not a change you did not notice.
tell: ている + いつの間にか a change: 〜うちに. A sudden break-in would be 最中に.

s: A「田中さんとは最初、仲が悪かったんだよね？」B「うん。でも、一緒に仕事を（　　）、だんだんお互いのことがわかるようになったんだ。」
en: A: You and Tanaka did not get on at first, right? B: Yes. But as we worked together, we gradually came to understand each other.
why: 〜ているうちに (change): over a period of doing something, a change crept in. だんだん〜ようになった is that change.
〜最中に is followed by a sudden interruption, not a change that grows over time.
〜たとたん marks a single instant. だんだん shows the change took a long time.
〜次第 is followed by a plan or a request, never a past change like わかるようになった.
tell: Over a stretch of time, だんだん〜ようになった: 〜ているうちに.

s: 円安が止まらず、輸入品の価格はここ一年（　　）。
en: With the yen still weakening, import prices have just kept rising over the past year.
why: Dictionary form + 一方だ: a change keeps moving in one direction. ここ一年 shows it has been going on for a while.
〜(よ)うとしている is the moment just before a change starts. ここ一年 says the rise is already well under way.
〜つつ 'while doing' joins two actions and cannot end a sentence. It needs a main clause after it.
〜た上で is a first step before a planned next step. It cannot end a sentence about prices.
tell: A change that keeps going one way and is already under way: 〜一方だ.

s: 若い人が都会へ出ていく流れが続いている。このままでは、地方の空き家は（　　）。
en: Young people keep leaving for the cities. If nothing changes, empty houses in the regions will just keep increasing.
c: 増えつつあっただろう
増えている最中だろう
why: 〜一方だろう: a guess that the change will keep going one way. このままでは asks for exactly this kind of forecast.
つつあった is past. このままでは looks ahead, so a past form cannot answer it.
〜ようとしていた is past and means 'was about to'. It cannot be a forecast after このままでは.
〜最中 is for a short activity that gets interrupted. A housing trend is not an activity.
tell: このままでは + a forecast of a one-way change: 〜一方だろう.

s: 長かった冬が終わり、庭の桜のつぼみが今にも（　　）。
en: The long winter is over, and the cherry buds in the garden are just about to open.
why: Volitional form + としている: the moment just before a change starts. 今にも 'any second now' asks for this.
〜つつある is a change already under way. 今にも points to the moment before it starts, not during it.
〜一方だ is a change that keeps going one way over time. A bud opening once is not a trend.
〜最中 is the middle of an activity that gets interrupted. It does not fit 今にも or a flower bud.
tell: 今にも + the moment before a change: 〜(よ)うとしている.

s: （ニュース）注目の両国首脳による会談が、今まさに（　　）。
en: (News) The closely watched summit between the two leaders is just about to begin.
c: 始まろうとしています
始めようとしています
始まっている最中です
why: 〜(よ)うとしている: the moment just before something starts. 今まさに + intransitive 始まる (会談が) fits.
始める is transitive and needs someone doing it (〜を始める). With 会談が as the subject, the intransitive 始まる is needed.
始まる happens in one moment, and 始まっている is the state after it began. 〜最中 needs an activity under way (会談の最中).
〜一方だ is a change that keeps going one way. A meeting starting is a single event.
tell: 今まさに + a one-moment change, just before it: 〜ようとしている. Watch 自他.

s: 医師たちの懸命な治療により、患者の容体は少しずつ（　　）。
en: Thanks to the doctors' hard work, the patient's condition is gradually improving.
c: 回復しようとしている
why: Verb stem + つつある: a change that is under way right now. 少しずつ shows a gradual change in progress.
〜(よ)うとしている is the moment just before a change starts. 少しずつ says the recovery has already begun.
〜かねない warns that something bad might happen. Recovery is good news, so it cannot take かねない.
〜つつ 'while doing' joins two actions and cannot end a sentence. Here it needs ある: つつある.
tell: 少しずつ + a change in progress, formal: 〜つつある.

s: 専門家によると、この地域の森林は温暖化の影響で年々（　　）という。
en: According to experts, the forests in this area are being lost year by year because of global warming.
c: 失われようとしている
why: Passive + つつある: the forests are in the middle of being lost. 年々 shows a change already in progress.
〜ようとしている is the moment just before a change starts. 年々 says the loss has been going on for years.
失う is active and needs an object (〜を失う). 森林は is the thing being lost, so the passive 失われる is needed.
〜最中 is the middle of a short activity that gets interrupted. A trend over many years does not fit.
tell: 年々 + a change in progress, in the passive: 失われつつある.

s: 当社では、製品の品質を（　　）、製造コストを下げる方法を検討しています。
en: We are looking for ways to cut production costs while keeping the quality of our products.
why: Verb stem + つつ: formal ながら. The same company keeps the quality and looks for savings at the same time.
〜たとたん is followed by a sudden surprise, not by a planned piece of work like 検討しています.
〜たかと思うと describes someone else you watched, and what follows is something that happened. 検討しています is our own ongoing plan.
〜最中に is the middle of a short activity that gets interrupted. Keeping quality is an ongoing aim, and nothing breaks in.
tell: Same subject, two things at once, formal: 〜つつ. A plan can follow it.

s: 私たちは今後も、お客様の声に耳を（　　）、より良いサービスを目指してまいります。
en: We will keep listening closely to our customers as we work toward better service.
why: Verb stem + つつ: formal 'while'. The same subject (私たち) listens and aims at the same time.
〜つつある describes a change in progress and ends a clause. Listening is an action, and a second action follows, so plain つつ is needed.
〜かと思うと is for watching someone else, and it bans intentions after it. Here 私たち state their own plan.
〜うちに (change) is followed by a change that crept in. It cannot be followed by a stated goal like 目指してまいります.
tell: Formal speech, same subject, two actions together: 〜つつ.

s: 大きな病気を（　　）、健康の本当のありがたさに気づくことができた。
en: Only after going through a serious illness was I able to see how precious good health really is.
why: て形 + はじめて: only after the experience did a realisation come that was impossible before. 気づく is the classic verb after it.
〜た上で is followed by a planned, deliberate step. You cannot plan a realisation.
〜次第 is followed by a plan or a request, never a past event like 気づくことができた.
〜て以来 is followed by a state that has gone on until now (ずっと〜ている). 気づくことができた is a one-time realisation.
tell: An experience, then a realisation (気づく・わかる) that was impossible before: 〜てはじめて.

s: 実際に自分で店を（　　）、商売の難しさが身にしみてわかった。
en: Only after actually running a shop myself did I truly understand how hard business is.
c: 経営してみてはじめて
経営してみてからでないと
why: 〜てはじめて: only after doing it yourself did you understand. 身にしみてわかった is the new realisation.
〜た上で leads to a deliberate, planned step. Understanding is not something you choose to do.
〜て以来 needs a state that has continued until now (ずっと〜ている). わかった is a single realisation.
〜てからでないと must be followed by a negative (〜できない, 〜わからない). わかった is positive.
tell: Hands-on experience, then わかった for the first time: 〜てはじめて.

s: 契約内容を十分に（　　）、こちらの書類にご署名をお願いいたします。
en: Please check the terms of the contract thoroughly, and then sign this document.
why: た形 + 上で: a careful first step, then a deliberate second step. Checking the contract informs the signing.
〜たとたん cannot be followed by a request, and it brings a surprise, not a planned step.
〜て以来 is followed by a state that has lasted until now. A request cannot follow it.
〜かと思うと is for watching someone else, and it cannot be followed by a request.
cue: ご署名をお願いいたします
tell: A careful first step, then a request for the next step: 〜た上で.

s: 申し訳ございませんが、この件は私の一存では決めかねますので、上司と（　　）。
en: I am sorry, but I cannot decide this on my own, so I will discuss it with my manager and then get back to you.
c: 相談の上、改めてお返事いたします
相談したとたん、改めてお返事いたします
相談の上に、改めてお返事いたします
相談して以来、改めてお返事いたします
why: 名の上 (no で) is the stiff business form of 〜た上で: consult first, then reply. Same subject, planned second step.
〜たとたん bans the speaker's intention after it. お返事いたします is a promise.
〜上に means 'on top of that' and stacks two similar facts. Consulting and replying are steps in order, not a stack.
〜て以来 cannot be followed by a future action. お返事いたします is about the future.
cue: 私の一存では決めかねます
tell: Business promise: consult first, then act. 〜の上(で). 〜上に only stacks facts.

s: 詳しい日程が（　　）、改めてメールにてご連絡申し上げます。
en: As soon as the detailed schedule is fixed, I will contact you again by email.
why: Verb stem + 次第: as soon as X happens, I will do Y. It must be followed by an intention, like ご連絡申し上げます.
〜たとたん is followed by something unexpected. It bans the speaker's intention after it.
〜かと思うと describes something you watched happen, and it bans intention after it.
〜つつ joins two actions by the same subject. The schedule gets decided, but I send the email.
tell: As soon as X, then MY promised action: verb stem + 次第.

s: 現在、ご入金の確認がまだ取れておりません。ご注文の商品は、ご入金を（　　）。
en: We have not yet been able to confirm your payment. We will ship the item you ordered as soon as we confirm it.
c: 確認し次第、発送いたします
確認し次第、発送いたしました
確認したとたん、発送いたします
確認したかと思うと、発送いたします
why: 〜次第 + a promise about the future: as soon as payment is confirmed, we will ship. This is the standard business pattern.
〜次第 always looks forward, and the payment is not confirmed yet (まだ). A past ending like 発送いたしました cannot follow it.
〜たとたん is followed by an unexpected event. It cannot be followed by the speaker's own plan.
〜かと思うと is for watching someone else's actions. It cannot be followed by the speaker's own plan.
cue: まだ取れておりません
tell: 次第 + a future promise (〜いたします). Never a past ending after 次第.

s: 雨が（　　）、中断していた工事を再開する予定です。
en: We plan to restart the suspended building work as soon as the rain stops.
why: 〜次第 'as soon as' takes the verb stem: やむ becomes やみ次第. A plan (再開する予定) follows.
次第 does not follow the た形 in this meaning. やんだ次第 is not the 'as soon as' pattern.
次第 does not follow the dictionary form here. The stem is needed: やみ.
〜次第では means 'depending on' and follows a noun (天候次第では). It does not mean 'as soon as'.
tell: As soon as + a plan: verb ます-stem + 次第 (やみ次第).

s: 社会人に（　　）、一冊も小説を読んでいない。
en: I have not read a single novel since I started working.
why: て形 + 以来: from a past point until now, the same state has continued. 一冊も〜ていない is that state.
〜た上で is a careful first step before a planned second step. Not reading anything is not a planned step.
〜てからでないと means 'unless you do X first, you can't'. It needs 'cannot' after it, not a report of what has happened.
〜次第 looks forward and must be followed by a plan or a request. 読んでいない reports the time up to now.
tell: A past starting point + 一度も／一冊も〜ていない up to now: 〜て以来.

s: 兄は大学を卒業して以来、（　　）。
en: My older brother has lived in Tokyo ever since he graduated from university.
c: ずっと東京で暮らしている
来年から東京で暮らすつもりだ
一度東京で暮らしてみたい
why: 〜て以来 is followed by a state that has run from that past point until now. ずっと〜ている is exactly that.
〜て以来 cannot be followed by a future plan. 来年から〜つもりだ looks ahead.
A plain non-past action (暮らし始める) is not a continuing state. After 〜て以来 you need 〜ている, 〜ていない or ずっと.
A wish (〜てみたい) looks to the future. After 〜て以来 only a state that continues up to now is allowed.
tell: 〜て以来 + ずっと〜ている or 一度も〜ていない. Never a plan or a wish after it.

s: 上司の許可を（　　）、この予算を使うことはできません。
en: You cannot use this budget unless you get your manager's permission first.
why: て形 + からでないと: unless you do X first, Y cannot happen. The negative できません is required after it.
〜た上で is followed by a positive, deliberate action (使ってください). Here the ending is negative.
〜次第 'as soon as' is followed by a plan or a request. 'As soon as you get permission, you cannot use it' makes no sense.
〜て以来 describes a state since a past point. A rule about what you may do does not fit it.
tell: Do X first, or else a negative (できない・無理だ): 〜てからでないと.

s: A「この新しいシステム、今日から使ってもいいですか。」B「いや、研修を（　　）。」
en: A: Can I start using this new system today? B: No, I cannot let you use it until you have done the training.
c: 受けてからでないと、使ってもらうわけにはいかないんです
受けてからでないと、すぐ使ってもらえるんです
受けた上で、使ってもらうわけにはいかないんです
受けたとたん、使ってもらうわけにはいかないんです
why: 〜てからでないと + a negative ending. 〜わけにはいかない 'I can't very well' supplies that negative.
〜てからでないと must be followed by a negative. すぐ使ってもらえる is positive.
〜た上で leads into a positive, planned step. 'After the training, I can't let you use it' contradicts itself.
〜たとたん marks a sudden, unexpected event. It does not state a rule about what must come first.
tell: Unless X first + a negative ending (わけにはいかない・できない): 〜てからでないと.

s: この博物館には、恐竜の化石（　　）、貴重な展示品が数多くそろっている。
en: This museum has many valuable exhibits, dinosaur fossils among them.
why: 〜をはじめ names the leading example, then a group word that includes it (貴重な展示品が数多く).
〜に際して marks a one-off occasion (開会に際して). Dinosaur fossils are exhibits, not an occasion.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place (三年にわたって). Fossils are not a span.
〜を通じて means 'via' a go-between or 'throughout' a period. Neither fits a list of exhibits.
tell: A leading example + a group word that includes it (数多く・各国・など): 〜をはじめ.

s: あの旅館は、料理（　　）、サービスや設備など、すべてが申し分ない。
en: Everything about that inn is excellent, starting with the food and including the service and facilities.
why: 〜をはじめ puts the leading example first, then the rest of the group (サービスや設備など、すべて). The whole is praised.
〜を通じて means 'via' a go-between or 'throughout' a period. Food is neither, and it cannot open a list of good points.
〜に限り is the 'only' of notices (本日に限り). It cannot introduce a list of good points.
〜にわたって needs a large span (三日間にわたって). 料理 is not a span.
tell: X first, then the rest of the group (〜など、すべて): 〜をはじめ.

s: あの会社は面接官の（　　）高圧的で、入社したいという気持ちがすっかりなくなった。
en: At that company, even the interviewer's manner was overbearing, and I completely lost any wish to join.
why: 名 + からして: one detail already shows how bad the whole is. A complaint (高圧的) follows.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it that includes the first item (多くの〜, 各国). There is none here.
〜を通じて means 'via' a go-between. An attitude is not a channel you reach someone through.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. 態度 is not a span.
tell: One detail proves the whole is bad: 名 + からして + criticism.

s: この企画書はタイトル（　　）ありきたりで、中身にもあまり期待できそうにない。
en: Even the title of this proposal is unoriginal, so I do not expect much from the contents.
why: 〜からして: if even a minor part (the title) is this bad, the rest probably is too. Criticism follows.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it (タイトルをはじめ、すべてが). Here ありきたりで describes the title alone.
〜に限り is the 'only' of notices. The writer is not limiting anything, and 中身にも shows the doubt spreads.
〜を通じて means 'via' or 'throughout'. A title is not a channel or a period.
tell: A minor part (タイトル) is already bad, so the whole must be: 〜からして.

s: 台風による大雨は、九州から東北までの広い範囲（　　）、大きな被害をもたらした。
en: The heavy rain from the typhoon caused severe damage across a wide area, from Kyushu to Tohoku.
why: 〜にわたって covers a large span of place or time. 広い範囲 is exactly that kind of span.
〜に限って means 'on this one occasion, unusually'. A region is not an occasion.
〜をはじめ names a leading example of a group. 広い範囲 is not one member of a list.
〜に際して marks a one-off occasion (開会に際して). A stretch of land is not an occasion.
cue: 九州から東北までの広い範囲
tell: A big span of place, time or count + にわたって.

s: 十回（　　）話し合いの末、両社はようやく合意に達した。
en: After talks that went on for ten rounds, the two companies finally reached an agreement.
why: 〜にわたる + noun: a span of time, place or count. 十回 is a count, and 末 and ようやく show a long process.
〜を通じて 'throughout' needs a period of time (一年を通じて). A number of meetings is not a period.
〜に限る limits something to 'only' (十回に限る). That clashes with ようやく, which stresses how long it took.
〜をはじめとする needs a leading example of a group. 十回 is not a member of a list.
tell: A count, period or area + にわたる + noun: a long span.

s: この地方は年間（　　）降水量が少なく、晴れの日が多い。
en: This region gets little rain all year round and has many sunny days.
why: 〜を通じて (throughout): the same state holds for a whole long period. 年間を通じて is the set phrase.
〜に応じて means adjusting to something that varies (予算・年齢). 年間 does not vary, and the rainfall is not adjusted to anything.
〜をはじめ names a leading example of a group. 年間 is not a member of a list.
〜に限り is the 'only' of notices. 'Only for the year' makes no sense in a description of climate.
tell: A whole period + the same state all through it: 〜を通じて (年間を通じて).

s: この屋内プールは温水なので、季節を問わず一年（　　）泳ぐことができる。
en: This indoor pool is heated, so you can swim there all year round, whatever the season.
why: 〜を通して (throughout): the same state holds for the whole period. 季節を問わず confirms 'all year'.
〜をはじめ names a leading example of a group. 一年 is a period, not a member of a list.
〜からして picks a small detail to criticise the whole. The sentence is not a criticism.
〜に際して marks a one-off occasion. 一年 is a whole period, not an occasion.
tell: A whole period, same state all through: 一年を通して.

s: 彼とは直接の面識がなかったため、共通の友人（　　）連絡を取った。
en: I did not know him personally, so I got in touch through a mutual friend.
why: 〜を通して (via): through a go-between person or medium. A mutual friend links you to him.
〜をはじめ names a leading example and then a group word. There is no group here.
〜からして picks a small detail to criticise the whole. Nothing is being criticised.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. A friend is not a span.
cue: 直接の面識がなかった
tell: Reaching someone through a person in between: 〜を通して.

s: 弊社の新製品に関する情報は、今後もホームページ（　　）随時お知らせしてまいります。
en: We will keep sharing news about our new products on our website whenever there is an update.
why: 〜を通じて (via): information reaches people through a medium. A website is that kind of channel.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. A website is a channel, not a span.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it (ホームページをはじめ、各種SNSで). None follows here.
〜に際して marks a one-off occasion. A website is not an occasion, and 随時 means 'whenever needed', not one time.
cue: お知らせしてまいります
tell: Information sent through a medium (ホームページ・SNS・テレビ): 〜を通じて.

s: 選手たちは最後まで力の（　　）戦い抜き、観客から大きな拍手を受けた。
en: The players fought with everything they had to the very end and got huge applause from the crowd.
why: 名の + 限り: to the full limit of something. 力の限り 'with all one's strength' is the set phrase.
〜の最中 is the middle of an activity that gets interrupted. 力 is not an activity.
〜のうちに needs a period that will end. 力 is not a period of time.
〜の際 is a formal 'when' for an event or action. 力 is neither.
tell: To the full limit: 力の限り, できる限り, 知っている限り.

s: この件について私が把握している（　　）情報を、すべて報告書にまとめました。
en: I have put every piece of information I have on this matter into the report.
why: 〜ている限りの + noun: all of it, up to the limit of what I have. It matches すべて.
〜限りでは hedges a judgement (as far as I know, X seems true). Here the writer reports their own action, not a hedged judgement.
〜限りは means 'as long as' and links two lasting states. It cannot describe a noun like 情報.
〜に限って follows a noun (今日に限って), not a verb, and means 'of all times'.
tell: Verb + 限りの + noun = all of it, to the limit (知っている限りの情報).

s: 今日は私のおごりだから、好きな（　　）注文していいよ。
en: It is my treat today, so order as much as you like.
why: 好きなだけ: as much as you like. 〜だけ marks the full amount you want.
〜うちに means 'while the chance lasts'. 'While you like it, order' does not make sense.
〜最中 is the middle of an activity. 好きな is a feeling, not an activity.
〜限りでは needs an information word before it (知っている, 調べた). 好きな is not one.
tell: 好きなだけ・〜たいだけ・〜るだけ: as much as you want or can.

s: A「締め切りまであと一週間しかないけど、大丈夫？」B「うーん、とにかく（　　）やってみます。」
en: A: There is only a week left until the deadline. Will you be OK? B: Hmm, I will just do as much as I can.
why: Potential verb + だけ + the same verb: do as much as you can (やれるだけやる). The repeated verb is the signal.
やれた is past, but B is talking about what to do from now on. The potential form must stay non-past.
〜うちに (change) is followed by a change that crept in, not a plan like やってみます.
〜次第 'as soon as' needs something that will happen first. 'As soon as I do it, I will try doing it' makes no sense.
tell: Same verb twice, potential form first: やれるだけやる = as much as I can.

s: 本日午後六時までにご来店のお客様（　　）、全品二割引きとさせていただきます。
en: Customers who visit the store by 6 p.m. today will get 20% off everything.
why: 名 + に限り: only this group gets the special treatment. It is the standard phrase in shop notices.
〜に限らず means 'not only'. It would make the 6 p.m. cut-off pointless, since everyone would get the discount.
〜限りでは needs an information word before it (調べた限りでは) and hedges a judgement. A shop offer is not a hedge.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. A group of customers is not a span.
tell: Shop notice + a cut-off group that gets an offer: 〜に限り.

s: 先着五十名様（　　）、記念品を差し上げます。
en: Only the first fifty visitors will receive a commemorative gift.
why: 名 + に限り: only that group qualifies. 先着 'first to arrive' already sets the limit.
〜にわたって covers a long span of time, place or repeated events. A group of fifty guests is not a span.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it that includes the first item. The sentence goes straight to the gift.
〜からして uses a small detail to criticise the whole. A gift offer is not a criticism.
tell: Notice + a limited group (先着〜名様・予約の方): 〜に限り.

s: （館内放送）開館記念日の今日（　　）。
en: (Announcement) Today only, on our opening anniversary, admission is free.
c: に限り、入館料が無料となります
に限って、入館料が無料となるはずがありません
の限りでは、入館料が無料となります
である限り、入館料が無料となります
why: 〜に限り + the special rule that applies: today only, admission is free. This is the official notice pattern.
〜に限って + はずがない is for a trusted person who would never do wrong (彼に限って). 今日 is not a person, and an announcement does not deny its own offer.
〜限りでは needs an information word (調べた, 知っている) and hedges a judgement. An announcement is not a hedge.
〜である限り means 'as long as' a lasting state holds. A single day is not a lasting state.
tell: Announcement + a one-time exception: 〜に限り + what applies. に限って〜はずがない is for a trusted person.

s: このチームは、今のエースが（　　）、優勝を狙えるだろう。
en: As long as their current ace is on the team, they can aim for the title.
why: Non-past state + 限り: as long as X holds, Y holds. While the ace is there, the title is possible.
〜限りでは needs an information word (見た, 聞いた) and limits where a judgement comes from. いる is not information.
〜限り 'as long as' needs the present form before it. いた (past) breaks the condition.
〜に限って follows a noun (今日に限って). It cannot follow いる, and it means 'of all times'.
tell: As long as a state holds (present form) + 限り: いる限り.

s: 本人が心から（　　）、同じ失敗を繰り返すだろう。
en: Unless he truly reflects on it himself, he will probably make the same mistake again.
why: ない形 + 限り = unless. As long as he does not reflect, the same mistake will come back.
〜限りでは needs an information word (調べた, 見た) and hedges a judgement. 反省しない is not information.
〜限り is a condition, so the verb before it stays non-past. 反省しなかった breaks it.
〜次第 means 'as soon as'. 'As soon as he reflects, he will repeat the mistake' is the opposite of the meaning.
tell: ない形 + 限り = unless, then a forecast: 〜ない限り〜だろう.

s: プロの選手（　　）、結果で評価されるのは当然のことだ。
en: As long as you are a professional athlete, it is only natural to be judged on results.
why: 名 + である + 限り: as long as you are X. A noun needs である before 限り.
名の限り means 'to the full limit of' (力の限り). It does not mean 'as long as you are'.
だ cannot come before 限り. A noun takes である: 選手である限り.
〜にしては sets up a surprise: 'for X, it is unexpectedly Y'. 当然のことだ says the result is expected, so they clash.
tell: Noun + である限り = as long as you are X. Not だ, not の.

s: 私の（　　）限りでは、そのような方針の変更はまだ正式に発表されていません。
en: As far as I know, no such change in policy has been officially announced yet.
why: An information verb + 限りでは: 'as far as my knowledge goes'. 知っている is the standard choice.
知らない is the opposite of an information source. 'As far as I don't know' makes no sense.
〜ようとする means 'try to'. Trying to know is not a source of information.
〜つつ cannot come before 限り. 知りつつ means 'even though I know' and links to a new clause.
cue: まだ正式に発表されていません
tell: Info verb (知っている・調べた・聞いた) + 限りでは + a careful statement.

s: ニュースで（　　）、事故の原因はまだわかっていないようだ。
en: From what I saw on the news, the cause of the accident still does not seem to be known.
why: 見た + 限りでは: the claim is limited to what I saw. A hedged judgement (〜ようだ) follows.
〜たとたん is followed by a sudden, unexpected event. A hedged judgement about a cause is not an event.
〜た上で is followed by a deliberate action by the same person. 〜ようだ is a judgement, not an action.
〜ているうちに (change) is followed by a change that crept in. Here nothing changes, there is just a judgement.
tell: Info source (見た・聞いた) + 限りでは + a hedge (〜ようだ・〜ない).

s: 社内で（　　）、新しい制度に反対している社員はほとんどいないようです。
en: From what I have heard asking around the office, hardly any staff seem to oppose the new system.
c: 聞いて回った限りでは
聞いて回ったとたんに
why: 〜た限りでは: 'as far as what I heard tells me'. The source is limited, so a hedge (〜ようです) follows.
〜たとたんに is followed by a sudden event, not a careful judgement about the whole office.
〜次第 looks forward to a plan or a request. 〜ようです reports a judgement about now.
〜限りは 'as long as' links two lasting states. 'As long as I keep asking, nobody opposes it' makes no sense.
cue: ほとんどいないようです
tell: What I gathered (聞いて回った・調べた) + 限りでは + a hedged report.

s: いつもは時間に正確な部長が、今朝（　　）一時間も遅れて出社してきた。
en: Our manager is always on time, but this morning of all mornings he came in a whole hour late.
why: 名 + に限って: normally X, but on this one occasion it was different. いつもは is the signal.
〜に限らず means 'not only this morning'. That clashes with いつもは時間に正確, which says he is normally on time.
〜限りでは needs an information word (見た, 聞いた). 今朝 is not a source of information.
〜からして uses a small detail to criticise the whole. 今朝 is a time, not a detail of something.
tell: いつもは X, but this time unusually Y: 〜に限って.

s: A「あれ、今日は自分でお弁当作ってきたの？」B「うん。いつもはコンビニなんだけど、今日（　　）早起きできたんだ。」
en: A: Oh, did you make your own lunch today? B: Yes. I usually get something from the convenience store, but today, for once, I managed to get up early.
why: 名 + に限って (unusually): the normal pattern changed just this once. Here the change is a good one.
〜に限らず means 'not only today'. That clashes with いつもはコンビニ, which says B does not usually manage this.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. 今日 is a single day.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it that includes the first item. There is none.
tell: いつもは〜けど + today, for once: 今日に限って. Not always bad luck.

s: 新しい白いシャツを着た日に（　　）、うっかりカレーをこぼしてしまう。
en: It is always on the day I wear a new white shirt that I spill curry on myself.
why: 日に限って: precisely on that day, bad luck strikes. 〜てしまう shows the speaker's frustration.
〜に対して aims an action or attitude at a target (客に対して丁寧だ). A day is not a target, and nothing is aimed at it.
〜に際して marks a formal, one-off occasion (開会に際して). It does not mean 'of all days'.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. 日 here is one day, not a span.
tell: On exactly the day I do X, bad luck (〜てしまう): 〜日に限って.

s: A「まだ帰らないの？」B「今日は早く帰ろうと思ってたのに、そういう日（　　）トラブルが起きるんだよね。」
en: A: Aren't you going home yet? B: I meant to leave early today, but trouble always comes up on days like that.
why: そういう日に限って: on exactly the kind of day I need things to go well, trouble comes. A complaint about bad luck.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place (三日間にわたって). One kind of day is not a span.
〜からして uses a small detail to criticise the whole. A day is not a detail of something.
〜を通して 'throughout' needs a long period (一年を通して). One day is too short, and the meaning here is 'precisely then'.
tell: I wanted X today, and of course trouble: そういう日に限って.

s: タクシーを拾いたい時（　　）。
en: Just when you want to catch a taxi, not a single one comes by.
c: に限って、一台も通らない
に際して、一台も通らない
に限って、一台も通らないはずがない
限りは、一台も通らない
why: 〜時に限って + a bad result: precisely when you need a taxi, none comes. This is the bad-luck complaint.
〜に際して marks a formal one-off occasion with an event noun (出発に際して). It does not follow 時, and it cannot voice bad luck.
〜に限って + はずがない is for a trusted person who surely would not do wrong (彼に限って). A moment in time is not a person you trust.
〜限りは 'as long as' takes a plain verb or adjective form directly (拾いたい限りは). It cannot follow the noun 時, and the meaning is wrong.
tell: When I need X + に限って + a bad result. はずがない belongs to the trusted-person meaning.

s: あんなにまじめな田中さん（　　）、会社のお金を勝手に使うはずがない。
en: Tanaka is so conscientious. He of all people would never use company money without permission.
why: Trusted person + に限って + はずがない: X of all people would never do that.
〜に対して marks the target of an action (田中さんに対して失礼だ). Here 田中さん is the one who would act, not the target.
〜をはじめ needs a group word after it (田中さんをはじめ、社員の皆さん). There is no group here.
〜にわたって needs a large span of time or place. A person is not a span.
tell: A trusted person + に限って + はずがない／わけがない.

s: A「山田さん、大事な書類をなくしたらしいよ。」B「えっ、几帳面な山田さん（　　）。何かの間違いじゃない？」
en: A: I hear Yamada lost some important documents. B: What? Careful Yamada would never make a mistake like that. Surely there has been a mix-up.
c: に限って、そんなミスをするわけがないよ
に限って、そんなミスをしたに違いないよ
に限って、そんなミスをするわけにはいかないよ
の限りでは、そんなミスをするわけがないよ
why: Trusted person + に限って + わけがない: B refuses to believe it. 何かの間違い confirms the denial.
This に限って must end in a denial. 〜に違いない accepts the mistake, which clashes with 何かの間違いじゃない？
〜わけにはいかない means 'cannot very well do it' about a choice someone faces. B is denying a fact, which needs わけがない.
〜の限りでは limits a claim to a source of information (調査の限りでは). A person is not an information source.
cue: 何かの間違いじゃない
tell: A trusted person + に限って + わけがない／はずがない: X of all people would never.
